summary: @ornikar/repo-config-react@13.0.9 ships obfuscated preinstall that downloads Bun and executes an opaque compiled payload
details: Version 13.0.9 introduces a `preinstall` lifecycle hook (`node setup.mjs`) that is heavily obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style `_0xNNNN` identifiers and string-lookup dispatchers (e.g. `_0x19328d.YCZJE(execFileSync,...)`). At install time it constructs a platform-specific URL for the Bun runtime v1.3.13 (`https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip`), downloads and unzips it into a temporary directory, marks the binary executable via `chmodSync(..., 493)`, and then invokes that Bun binary against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB opaque Bun-compiled CJS bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) whose literals are encoded through a numeric lookup table (`n7gIxM`) and a shift-rotate decoder (`WV8StW`), rendering the executed code unreadable to Node-oriented scanners. The package's declared purpose is a shared React repo-config; the CHANGELOG through 13.0.7 documents only version bumps and Node upgrades, with no reference to Bun, `setup.mjs`, or `math_init.js`. Fetching a second JS runtime and executing an obfuscated compiled bundle on `npm install` is inconsistent with the declared purpose and prior release history, and matches the alternate-runtime dropper pattern used to evade static analysis.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
